findings.title: Backup-code redemption is not atomic
findings.body: Two login requests can read the same backup-code list before either update completes. Both can validate the same code, then both write a list with that code nulled and both issue authenticated sessions. This makes a supposedly single-use recovery code reusable under concurrent requests. Consume the code with an atomic conditional update or equivalent serialization, and reject the request if another redemption already changed the list.

findings.title: OAuth 2FA login has no backup-code option
findings.body: The new “Lost access” control is only rendered in `TwoFactorFooter`; the login page instead renders `ExternalTotpFooter` when `totpEmail` is present. OAuth login can route a user with 2FA enabled to this `totpEmail` flow, so that user cannot select or submit a backup code and is locked out if they lack their authenticator.

findings.title: Backup-code authentication is not tested
findings.body: The added test only checks that backup codes can be displayed, copied, and downloaded; it never redeems one during login or verifies that a redeemed code is rejected on reuse. Those are the core authentication and single-use guarantees of this feature, so regressions in the new credential-validation and persistence path can pass the suite unnoticed.
